title: Seven Thousand Towers, Nobody Wrote Down Why

segments.narration: Sardinia has seven thousand stone towers and no written explanation. They are called nuraghi. Cones of stacked dark stone, the tallest about twenty metres.
They went up in the Bronze Age, from roughly the eighteenth century BC onward. Individual blocks run to several tons each.
Nothing bonds them. The walls hold on the weight of their own stones, leaning inward until they close into a dome overhead. And nobody knows what they were for.
Fortresses. Chiefs' houses. Temples. Meeting halls. Archaeologists have argued every one of those, and there is still no agreement.
Then a 2002 survey measured the doorways. A great many of them face the winter solstice sunrise, which means whatever else these towers were, somebody was lining them up with the sky.

candidates.text: Sardinia has seven thousand stone towers and no written explanation
candidates.why: The scale and the silence in one line - thousands of buildings, zero records.

candidates.text: Each block weighs tons and nothing holds them together
candidates.why: Leads on the engineering, but doesn't say what the thing is.

candidates.text: Ten thousand of these were built. Nobody said what for
candidates.why: Strong loop, but 'these' means nothing to a cold viewer.

choice.reason: It names the place, the number and the mystery in ten words, and the open loop - why build seven thousand of anything? - is exactly what the last segment half-answers.
